speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Given your symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, I need to know if you have noticed any recent unintentional weight loss in pounds or kilograms.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. ESR: Not included in provided data.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning, as fixed, painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is a classic "B症状" (B symptoms) presentation often associated with malignancy rather than just an infection. Did you experience any persistent cough, hemoptysis, or shortness of breath alongside the weight loss?

REQUEST TEST: LDH and Tumor Markers; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT and Ultrasound of the Neck.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated. CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Findings: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (specifically, the presentation of massive, fixed supraclavicular and mediastinal lymphadenopathy with B-symptoms and elevated LDH is highly suggestive of a lymphoproliferative malignancy).

REQUEST IMAGES: Please review the Ultrasound of the Neck for the specific characteristics of the supraclavicular node to confirm biopsy planning.

Do you have a history of alcohol consumption or any recent viral illnesses before these symptoms started?
